rail_guard.text: Connolly Station. Trains to every Irish station you've visited. Please mind the gap, the step and your dignity.
Hop aboard. The Wildlore rail runs to any town you have visited on this island. Where to?

sailor.text: Back to Holyhead, is it? The Ulysses is warming her engines, and a seagull has already bagged the best seat.

then.text: The launch was a triumph. Eleven people stayed for the cake. Nobody stayed for the speech. Metrics are metrics.
If you do come to Kilkenny, do bring the castle's measurements. I've been rounding up.

else.text: A stage on the quays. A banner reads IRELAND'S ANCIENT EAST EXPERIENCE (tm), with a smaller line underneath: terms apply. A string quartet is playing something that is nearly a reel.
Dia dhuit, Dublin! That's 'hello' for the visitors. It's in the brief. I'm told to say it with warmth.
Ireland is a land of five thousand years of heritage. And now, at last, it comes with a booking system.
Newgrange. Tara. Glendalough. Kilkenny Castle. Every stone, every ring fort, every holy well. Available in three tiers: Bronze, Silver and Ancient.
A Warden hands you a lanyard. It says GUEST on it, with a small barcode and a smaller smiley face.
The Wardstone will keep the stones quiet and presentable. No humming during the tour. No ghosts, unless pre-booked.
Her eyes land on you and narrow, like a woman checking a spreadsheet.
Oh. You. The unlicensed walker, from the incident reports. You're taller than the file said.
I won't fight you here. It's a launch. There's cake. Go and enjoy Dublin. Kilkenny, if you must. The castle would make a lovely Members' Lounge.
Slán abhaile. That's 'safe home', and I mean it. In a purely contractual sense.

then.text: Rain on the Ha'penny Bridge. Everyone's walking fast now, so I'm playing fast. Teamwork.
Sun on the Liffey! The whole city's in a good mood. Tips are up, so's the tempo.
Dusk is the best time on the bridge. The lamps come on and everyone goes soft.

bridge_busker.text: {greeting} The Ha'penny Bridge is a lovely spot to play. Everyone slows down on it, and the echo does half my work.
A halfpenny to cross, they charged. I do it for a euro and a smile. Or a smile and a euro. The smile's optional.

then.text: Grand soft day, as we say in Dublin. Perfect weather for an old library and a very old book.
You're up early! The queue for the Book of Kells hasn't even woken up yet.

kells_guide.text: The Book of Kells is a gospel written out by monks around 800 AD, with the most gorgeous illustrations: cats, mice, peacocks, and a lot of knotwork.
It is kept under glass in the Old Library. They turn a page every so often so it doesn't get bored. Honestly.

then.text: Ducks don't mind the rain. They look at me like I'm the strange one for having an umbrella.
Early breakfast for the ducks. They're very punctual. I'm the one in my slippers.

green_duck.text: These ducks know me. They know my pockets, my cardigan, and my heavy sighs.
St Stephen's Green had a different feel, once. It was a common for grazing cattle. Now it's a common for grazing sandwiches.

then.text: That wind would take the hat clean off you. I'm just saying, mind the hat.

pub_regular.text: {greeting} Temple Bar's got more pubs per square foot than anywhere I know. I'm not recommending that, it's an observation.
Sláinte, they say, which is 'health'. It means a toast. I'm told it also means 'one more'. Both are true on the same evening.

then.text: Fog in the Phoenix Park. The deer step out of it like ghosts. Very polite ghosts.
Windy one. The deer are all huddled under the trees, giving out about it.

deer_keeper.text: The deer in the park are fallow deer, spotted in summer, and they've lived here since the 1660s. They're very relaxed.
You can walk right up to them, but I'd advise against it. They look fluffy. They're not for hugs.

fawn.text: It looks at you with the calm of a deer that has seen several hundred tourists today. You are the nicest of them.

gate_dublin_south.text: Roadworks. The M11 is being resurfaced with a heritage-compliant finish. It's very fancy tarmac.
Declan at the hurling hall says he'll sort the permits, if you win him over. Everyone in Dublin knows Declan.

gate_dublin_north.text: North road's closed for the Ancient East launch. The sign says 'Experience in progress'.
Try the long way round, via the west. You may find the closure lifts by the time you get there.

dublin_lamplighter.text: Some of the old lamps round Merrion Square are still gas, you know. Somebody's got to keep them happy.
Dublin by lamplight. The Georgian doors all glow red and blue and yellow. Like sweets in a jar.
Quiet streets, warm lamps, and a fox having a look at me. That's my night sorted.

dublin_fox_watcher.text: Dublin's full of foxes at night. They're more Dublin than I am, and I'm from Phibsborough.
Red torch, see? Foxes don't mind red light. They just carry on with their business.
Saw one trot over O'Connell Bridge last week like he was late for a bus.
